claims.text: Fluctuations in local shear-fault energy govern the strength of multi-component concentrated alloys.
Fluctuations in local shear-fault energy govern the deformation or failure behavior of multi-component concentrated alloys.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations affect mechanical behavior by influencing dislocation motion.
The initial alloy contains varying local chemical ordering and grain boundaries.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations can be introduced in a controlled comparison.
Dislocation patterning is a structural mediator of the proposed mechanical response.
Local chemical ordering is a structural mediator of the proposed mechanical response.
Introducing local shear-fault-energy fluctuations will increase strength relative to an alloy without such fluctuations.
Introducing local shear-fault-energy fluctuations will alter deformation or failure behavior relative to an alloy without such fluctuations.
The proposed effects depend on temperature and loading conditions.
An alloy without local shear-fault-energy fluctuations can serve as the baseline.

The hypothesis would be falsified if controlled simulations found no significant difference in strength or deformation/failure behavior between alloys with and without local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
